queue.name: Haditha–Kirkuk Oil Pipeline (Basra–Ceyhan corridor connector)
queue.note: Missing north-south link that would tie the existing Basra-Haditha trunk (P0544, under construction) to the existing Kirkuk-Ceyhan line (P0547, operating); no roster PID covers a Haditha-to-Kirkuk segment. Under feasibility study by a Chevron/Capital TI (US)/UCC Holding (Qatar) consortium per Iraqi cabinet approval (5 Jul 2026), alongside an independent Mar 2026 Turkish proposal (Energy Minister Bayraktar) to extend Kirkuk-Ceyhan south to Basra. Studies due end-2026; no route/length/diameter/cost fixed yet.

evidence.note: Iraq cabinet (5 Jul 2026) approved non-binding heads-of-agreement with Chevron/Capital TI/UCC consortium for feasibility studies comparing Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan vs Basra-Haditha-Baniyas routes.
Oil minister Basim Khudair describes 'a crude pipeline system linking Basra with Faysh Khabur and Turkey's Ceyhan'; ~2 million bpd capacity cited by unnamed officials.
Consortium named to build pipeline network from Basra to Fishkhabur, extending onward to Ceyhan (Turkey) or Baniyas (Syria).
Cabinet approved (5 Jul 2026) agreement between Basra Oil Company and consortium for feasibility studies; no signed construction contract yet.
Route 1 described: Basra -> Haditha -> Kirkuk -> Ceyhan (Turkey).
Feasibility studies due end-2026, construction start possibly 2027.
Describes new build as 'a pipeline from southern Iraq to Kirkuk in the north,' with Kirkuk-Ceyhan/Kirkuk-Baniyas legs treated as existing infrastructure.
Notes the KBR consultancy contract is specifically for the Basra-Haditha segment, distinct from the Haditha-Kirkuk extension.
Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar: 'let us extend this pipeline, which currently runs up to Kirkuk, all the way to Basra' -- independent corroboration from the Turkish side.
Turkiye aims to extend the pipeline south from Kirkuk to the Basra Gulf region within a year, raising capacity to 2.5 million bpd.
Confirms the missing link is the Basra/Haditha-to-Kirkuk connection, not the already-existing Kirkuk-Ceyhan leg.
Summarizes the Basra-Haditha trunk and Oil Ministry intent to add branches from Haditha, distinct from the resumed Kirkuk-Ceyhan flow.

queue.name: Haditha–Baniyas Oil Pipeline
queue.note: New branch proposed off the Basra-Haditha trunk (P0544) toward Baniyas, Syria. Distinct origin (Haditha, not Kirkuk) from the existing Kirkuk-Baniyas family (P0546/P5277/P5278/P5279/P7913), which is being pursued as a separate revival of old infrastructure. Feasibility study only as of Jul 2026; no route/length/diameter fixed.

evidence.note: Iraq oil ministry announced (25 Jan 2026) feasibility studies for a pipeline linking Haditha to Syria's Baniyas terminal, building on the Basra-Haditha pipeline as launch point.
Oil Minister Hayan Abdul-Ghani chaired a meeting (28 Jan 2026) on the implementation plan for the Haditha-Baniyas crude pipeline.
Construction started on Basra-Haditha trunk (1 May 2026); Oil Ministry plans branches from Haditha toward Jordan (Aqaba) and toward Baniyas (Syria).
Iraqi News Agency: Iraq considers new oil pipeline to Syrian port of Baniyas (page blocked automated fetch; not independently re-read beyond substring verification).
Names 'Basra-Haditha-Baniyas route, targeting the Syrian Mediterranean coast' as one of two alternatives under the same Jul 2026 feasibility-study agreement.
Oil minister describes 'a branch from Haditha to Syria's Baniyas' alongside the Ceyhan option.
Describes pipeline network extending to 'the Syrian port of Baniyas' as an alternative outlet to Ceyhan.

queue.name: Samawa Refinery–Samawa Power Plant Fuel Oil Pipeline
queue.note: 6km/6-inch fuel oil pipeline from Samawa Refinery to Samawa Combined-Cycle Power Plant in Al-Muthanna, brought online Apr 2025, replacing tanker-truck delivery. No roster row connects a Muthanna refinery to a power plant; same class as existing tracked refinery/pipeline-to-power-plant lines (Ahdeb-Wassit, Strategic Pipeline-Musaiab, Strategic Pipeline-Al-Khairat) but a different, independently sourced location.

evidence.note: Oil Pipelines Company brought online a 6 km, 6-inch fuel oil pipeline linking Samawa Refinery to Samawa Combined-Cycle Power Plant.

queue.name: Ratawi (Artawi)–PS1 Export Pipeline
queue.note: New 30km, 24-inch TotalEnergies export line connecting the Ratawi (Artawi) oilfield/CPF1 to the PS-1 pumping station in North Rumaila, started up Feb 2026 as Ratawi expands from 60,000 to 100,000 b/d. No existing PS1-linked line (Zubair 2-PS1 P5285, PS1-Az Zubayr P6172, PS1-Fao P5282, PS1-Tuba P6180) matches this origin or spec.

evidence.note: TotalEnergies started up a new 24-inch, 30-km export pipeline connecting Ratawi oilfield to PS-1 pumping station.
Confirms the Artawi-PS1 export pipeline was 95% finalised as part of TotalEnergies' $27bn four-project Iraq megaproject (GGIP).
